correctness.rationale: For every odd prime power q≥3, e≥2 and admissible r, the congruence rℓ_h≡1 mod L and gcd(r,q−1)=1 imply gcd(r,q^e−1)=1 and F_{r,a}=(x^{q^h}+ax)∘(x^r). The embeddings make Frobenius a single e-cycle when gcd(h,e)=1, so det_{F_q}(T)=N(a)+(-1)^(e−1)=N(a)−(-1)^e. Sign of an invertible F_q-linear map is χ_q(det); sign of x→x^r on the cyclic group F_Q^× equals 1 for Q≡3 mod4 and (-1)^((r−1)/2) for Q≡1 mod4 by CRT and unit strata. Surjective norm fibers each have size L. The complete shifted χ-sum over F_q^×\{(-1)^e} is −χ_q((-1)^(e+1)), yielding the exact nonzero signed imbalance and boxed counts. Independent enumerators verified actual 2-dimensional extensions for p=3,5,7 and r=1,5,7,17, and power-map parity across eight even Q−1 moduli; source VERIFY.py was inspected, not accepted merely from its log. The conclusion is universal by algebra, not by finite tests.

value.rationale: An established complete classification of admissible permutation binomials makes alternating-group membership and its coefficient distribution a natural unresolved refinement. This theorem gives a closed sign for every eligible coefficient and establishes the same strict magnitude L of parity imbalance for all odd q, all extension degrees and all admissible fixed exponents, including complete one-parity families for q=3. It characterizes an exact invariant beyond bijectivity and unsigned function counts. The deductions use standard parity lemmas and a short character sum, so the contribution is an elementary but independently useful fixed-family quantitative classification, not a general theorem on permutation groups or a new classification of bijectivity.
